house.description: Health plan coverage of conversion therapy for minors and vulnerable adults prohibited, and commissioner of human rights required to protect Minnesotans from conversion therapy.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Judiciary Finance and Civil Law

additions: [62A.195] PROHIBITION ON COVERAGE OF CONVERSION THERAPY FOR MINORS AND VULNERABLE ADULTS.
Subdivision 1.
Definitions.
(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.
(b) "Conversion therapy" has the meaning given in section 214.078, subdivision 1, paragraph (b).
(c) "Vulnerable adult" has the meaning given in section 626.5572, subdivision 21.
Subd. 2.
Prohibition.

A health plan that is offered, sold, issued, or renewed to Minnesota residents must not include coverage for conversion therapy for an enrollee under 18 years of age or for an enrollee who is a vulnerable adult.
EFFECTIVE DATE.
This section is effective January 1, 2027, and applies to health plans offered, sold, issued, or renewed on or after that date.

(c) The commissioner shall take all appropriate actions to protect Minnesotans from conversion therapy including, to the extent permissible, investigating charges and pursuing civil relief when the commissioner has reason to believe a mental health practitioner or mental health professional is engaging in unfair discriminatory practices. For purposes of this paragraph, "conversion therapy" has the meaning given in section 214.078, subdivision 1, paragraph (b).
